readings: MATCH is a combinational Mealy output: it changes in the same cycle as IN, so it is 1 at the same cycle as the last bit of 10011 (as stated).
MATCH is updated on the positive edge of CLK (as the sensitivity list 'positive edge of CLK' suggests), making it a registered output that appears one cycle after the last bit of 10011.
RST is an asynchronous, active-high reset: when RST is high, MATCH is forced to 0 immediately, independent of CLK.
RST is a synchronous, active-high reset: MATCH is set to 0 only on the next rising edge of CLK while RST is high.
RST is an asynchronous, active-low reset (nRST): MATCH is forced to 0 when RST is low.
After reset, the FSM goes to an idle state where no bits of the sequence have been matched, so MATCH is 0 until a full 10011 is seen.
The reset state is not defined, so it could reset to any of the sequence-detection states, potentially causing MATCH to be 1 for some inputs immediately after reset.
MATCH is updated on any change of IN (as stated), which is correct for a Mealy output.
MATCH is updated only on the positive edge of CLK (as also stated), which would ignore IN changes between clock edges and make the output effectively Moore-like or registered.
